propositions: A bare git repository created with `git init --bare` and pushed to immediately afterwards leaves a detached `git maintenance run` background process that concurrently rewrites the object database while `shutil.copytree` attempts to walk it, causing files (loose-object fanout directories and maintenance.lock) to vanish mid-copy.
The race is not limited to maintenance.lock; the concurrent repack prunes entire loose-object fanout directories (objects/2c, objects/2d, etc.), so ignoring `*.lock` does not fix the flake.

Pinning `receive.autogc=false`, `gc.autoDetach=false`, and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` on fixture bare remotes before they are used removes the concurrent mutator: `receive.autogc=false` prevents maintenance spawning entirely, and the autoDetach pins force any maintenance into the foreground so it completes before the triggering git command returns.

The new guard test `test_fixture_bare_remote_leaves_no_detached_upkeep_behind_a_push` asserts the mutator's absence directly from git's process trace under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, verifying no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`, with a `receive-pack` positive control to ensure the trace was actually recorded.
